why: A strong reference for turning a studio homepage into one immersive stage: the shell is built around a full-viewport scene, sparse copy, custom typography, and deliberate loader-to-experience boot behavior.

compositions.title: Single viewport scene shell
compositions.study: The page is organized around one `#Stage` container that claims the full viewport instead of behaving like a normal document scroll.
compositions.reuse: Use when a motion-led site should feel like entering one scene rather than browsing stacked sections.

compositions.title: Loader before scene boot
compositions.study: The HTML boot path preloads the main app script and treats the scene as a runtime that must be ready before the experience starts.
compositions.reuse: Use when cinematic pacing matters more than instant content dump, but keep fallback messaging visible.

assets.notes: The shell loads multiple weights of NB Architekt before the main app boot sequence.
assets.reuse: Treat typography as part of the stage system, not a last-minute decorative layer.

assets.notes: The viewport is reserved for a JS-driven stage rather than a static hero image.
assets.reuse: Plan scene ownership, boot timing, and mobile fallbacks before building visual motion.

motion.title: Boot into stage
motion.notes: The shell prioritizes an app preload and transitions into the runtime scene instead of rendering a static homepage first.
motion.fallback: When JS is unavailable, the page only exposes a direct enable-JS message, so this entry needs a later fallback review.

motion.title: Scene-led chaptering
motion.notes: The static shell hints at a stage that owns the viewport and likely swaps chapters inside one continuous scene.
motion.fallback: Not verified live; backfill with a browser pass before reusing the chapter model directly.

interactions.title: Pointer-safe scene container
interactions.study: The shell disables user selection, suppresses default touch behavior, and routes interaction through the stage container.
interactions.reuse: Use when the pointer should manipulate or explore the scene instead of selecting the page.

interactions.title: Runtime-owned interaction model
interactions.study: The page is architected as a JS application with its own unsupported-browser branch and iOS/mobile handling.
interactions.reuse: Treat device branches and capability checks as part of the interaction design, not only engineering cleanup.

implementation.notes: Static inspection showed a single stage container, touch suppression, custom font loading, and explicit unsupported-browser handling; the actual scene choreography still needs live browser backfill.
